attacker_pocs.name: split-tar-close-open-fallback
attacker_pocs.why: A two-node read client with open/read/close callbacks and no switch callback is the documented multi-volume fallback: client_switch_proxy closes the current node (which frees the buffer just returned by read) and opens the next. Bidding a split tar (uu filter enabled, 4096-byte blocks, header crossing the volume boundary) leaves client_avail/client_next aimed at that freed buffer; archive_read_data then memcpy's it. The patch zeroes those lengths only in the switcher branch, so archive_read_open_filenames is fixed and the regression test passes, but the close/open path is not. The upstream fix assigns client_total = client_avail = 0 after both branches, so the same callbacks do not reuse the freed buffer.

role_a_rationale: The real fix clears f->client_total and f->client_avail once, after both the switch-callback arm and the close/open fallback in client_switch_proxy. This commit places that same assignment only in the switcher arm, next to f->data = data2, and adds the upstream split-tar regression (archive_read_open_filenames, which always installs a switcher). That path matches the golden behavior (870 libarchive tests pass under ASan, including the new test and existing multivolume RAR/callback tests). The residual is the else arm: a public multi-node client that does not set a switch callback still frees the live read buffer in the closer and leaves client_avail/client_next unchanged, so the next body read is a heap use-after-free. The same PoC exits 0 on a build with the unconditional clear.
